news.headline: Kyler Murray ruled out; Carson Wentz starts for MIN
news.detail: The Vikings ruled Murray out with a hamstring strain, and Carson Wentz starts against BUF. The brief lists Murray as MIN's QB, so the model's numbers may not reflect this (reported Nov 5-9).

news.headline: MIN also without WR Jauan Jennings and RB Demond Claiborne
news.detail: Both were ruled out on the final report. Safety Theo Jackson is also out, and safety Jay Ward is questionable (Nov 7-9).

news.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins questionable; WR Joshua Palmer out
news.detail: Dawkins (ribs) did not practice all week and is questionable. Guard Alec Anderson (ankle) is also questionable. Palmer was ruled out and put on IR (Nov 7-9).

news.headline: James Cook has no injury tag; left last week's game late
news.detail: Cook practiced and carries no designation. One report says he got folded up on a tackle last week. Books have his rushing line near 84.5 yards, and the Bills plan a heavy workload (Nov 9).

news.headline: Wentz-led MIN offense is thin; one outlet leans to a low-scoring first half
news.detail: MIN is bottom three in the league in offensive EPA per play and success rate. One ESPN preview likes the first half under 22.5. Another says Wentz throws deeper but lacks mobility (Nov 9).

item_notes.NFL|likely|2026_09_BUF_MIN|winner|away||: The model's 54% likely assumes Kyler Murray at QB. He is out and Carson Wentz starts, so the model's number may be off.
item_notes.NFL|value|2026_09_BUF_MIN|total|under|||: A Wentz start and a weak MIN offense fit a lower total. Buffalo's offense scores a lot, so the Under is not clear-cut, and the edge over break-even is only 0.4 points.
item_notes.NFL|risky|2026_09_BUF_MIN|winner|home|||: The model's 46% for MIN was probably built with Murray, who is out. Jennings and Claiborne are also out, so this long shot looks weaker than listed.
item_notes.NFL|props_likely|2026_09_BUF_MIN|prop|at: Cook has no injury designation and the Bills plan to lean on him. Books set his rushing line around 84.5 yards, well above 50.
item_notes.NFL|props_risky|2026_09_BUF_MIN|prop|at: Cook's rushing line is about 84.5 yards, so 100+ needs a big night. Minnesota has allowed 100+ to two rushers this season, and one outlet is fading Cook against its run defense.

NFL.recap: Week 9 went well for picking winners: the model was right on 12 of 13 games, with only GB over NE wrong. Against the spread it did worse. It won 5 of the 13 spreads and was 8 of 12 on totals. The big misses were GB-NE (21.4 points off, 4 NE turnovers), JAX-BAL (17.5 off), HOU-LAC (18.1 off) and KC-NYJ (12.2 off). Those came from turnovers, finishing drives or things the stats don't show.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has mostly lost so far.
lessons.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won (CIN over BAL and DEN over KC won; PHI over DAL, NYG over NO, ATL over CHI, PHI over CAR, NE over CHI lost). No Week 9 game or the BUF-MIN game disagrees with the Vegas favorite, so no new cases.
lessons.test: On past seasons, take every game where the model's pick differs from the moneyline favorite. Compare its win rate and spread record with Vegas. Wait for 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
lessons.evidence: Before Week 9, 0 of 5 graded games with a gap of 4.9 or more won the over/under pick. Week 9 split: TB-CHI (gap 5.0) lost, CIN-ATL (gap 4.9) won. That makes it 1 of 7 at best. The Week 9 gap-4.2 game JAX-BAL won. Overall the over/under is 28-24.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by size of the total gap (under 2, 2-4, over 4). Check hit rate per group. Needs 20+ games in the large-gap group.

lessons.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
lessons.evidence: In 9 of the 16 games where the winner was wrong, the review names efficiency as the main reason. The new miss, GB-NE, came from turnovers (NE 4, GB 0). Week 9 blowouts split: KC-NYJ and LV-SF came from finishing drives and turnovers, while HOU-LAC, CIN-ATL and most of JAX-BAL had no stat explanation.
lessons.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

lessons.lesson: Long-shot picks (underdog winners and big-game props) hit a bit below the model's chances and lose units.
lessons.evidence: Underdog picks are 5 of 18 against 7.2 expected (-5.54 units). Big-game picks are 11 of 35 against 11.5 expected (-10.49 units). Combined, 16 of 53 against 18.7 expected. The big-game hit rate is now near expectation, so most of its unit loss comes from prices. The underdog gap is about 2 hits. Milestone picks are 30 of 39 against 29.1 expected (-3.41 units).
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for underdog winners and long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether the prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running a little below the model's chances.
lessons.evidence: 11 of 23 best-value picks hit this season, against 12.2 expected, at -2.00 units. The gap to expectation has shrunk from 2 hits to about 1. This week's Under 45.5 sits only 0.4 points over break-even.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks per edge group.

lessons.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
lessons.evidence: Average spread miss is 9.7 for the model against 8.9 for Vegas over 55 graded games. The model is 24-30-1 against the spread. Winners are 38 of 54 (70%). Week 9 went 5-8 against the spread.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week, over a full season. Also check ATS record by season. Do this before changing anything.

lessons.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas may come from lineup changes the model hasn't picked up.
lessons.evidence: DAL at PHI listed Hurts (on IR); DAL won 38-21 against the model's PHI by 3.9. PHI at WAS listed him again; WAS won 27-10 against the model's WAS by 3.3 (Vegas -6). This week the brief lists Kyler Murray for MIN, but he is out and Carson Wentz starts. The model has MIN at 46% against Vegas 36%. That is 3 known cases, well under 20.
lessons.test: On past seasons, flag games where a starting QB differed from the one in the model's inputs. Compare the model's margin error in those games with all others. Needs 20+ such games.

lessons.lesson: Most-likely-winner picks have fallen short of the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: 15 of 23 most-likely-winner picks hit this season, against 16.9 expected, at -3.77 units. The shortfall is about 2 hits. Overall winners are 38 of 54 (70%), so the model's winner calls look better than its pick-list results.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (70-79%, 80%+) and compare hit rate with the moneyline-implied chance. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

news.headline: Notre Dame may be missing five defensive starters again vs. Boston College
news.detail: Per reports on Nov. 9-10, linebacker Drayk Bowen, safety Brauntae Johnson and cornerback DJ McKinney are out. Linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are questionable. All five missed the win over Miami. The line is already Notre Dame -29.5.

news.headline: Georgia has a thin receiver room and a cornerback in doubt before Missouri
news.detail: On Nov. 9 Kirby Smart said Georgia is dinged up at wideout. Cornerback Ellis Robinson (thigh/hip) is a work in progress and wide receiver Craig Dandridge has a hamstring issue. Running back Chauncey Bowens is not at 100%. Quarterback Gunner Stockton is not listed on the latest report.

news.headline: Iowa's depth chart still lists two quarterbacks at the top
news.detail: The Week 11 depth chart (Nov. 9) shows Hank Brown and Jeremy Hecklinski as an either/or at quarterback. Iowa also lists LJ Phillips and Xavier Williams as an either/or at running back, and Williams pulled up limping against Northwestern. Brown played in the 24-10 win at Northwestern, so he looks available.

news.headline: UCF lost two running backs at Kansas; Arizona State starts a freshman QB
news.detail: Duke Watson left in a boot with a foot injury and Landen Chambers has an undisclosed injury, per Nov. 10 reports. UCF needs one more win for bowl eligibility. Arizona State's Week 10 report had freshman Jake Fette as the starting quarterback, with Mikey Keene probable as backup.

news.headline: Washington's Demond Williams is set to start at Michigan State
news.detail: A Nov. 10 report says Williams gets the start after reclaiming the job from Elijah Brown. Michigan State's Alessio Milivojevic returned from injury for a 15-6 win at Michigan last Saturday.

news.headline: Air Force used two quarterbacks in the win over Army
news.detail: Evan Medders returned from a turf toe injury and shared snaps with Kemper Hodges in the 24-21 win on Nov. 7. San José State is 5-5 and led by senior Luke Weaver.

College.recap: Week 10 went about as the model expected on winners, but it was weaker against the line. Of the 40 results shown, the model had 24 of 39 winners right, went 17-23 against the spread, and its totals picks went 14-25. Misses were big: Tulsa beat Tulane 60-10 (53 points off), Duke beat NC State 41-3 and Georgia won 42-7 at Ole Miss. Efficiency was the main reason in 14 of 26 misses of 8+ points. On the Top picks, Most likely winners are 22 of 24, Best value 12 of 30 and underdogs 10 of 29.

lessons.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up, and the model's totals picks overall have lost more than they won.
lessons.evidence: Weeks 8-9: over hit in 11 of 29 such games. Week 10 (40 results shown): 5 of 10 (UCF-Kansas, Oregon-Ohio State, Delaware-Kennesaw State, Tulsa-Tulane, North Carolina-UConn went over; Arizona State-Colorado, Air Force-Army, Notre Dame-Miami, Vanderbilt-Mississippi State, Duke-NC State did not). Combined 16 of 39 (41%). Season totals picks are 105-125 (46%); 14-25 in the Week 10 results shown.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Also compare the model's and Vegas's average total error. Need 20+ games per group.

lessons.lesson: Big misses are spread across several causes, but efficiency still leads.
lessons.evidence: Week 10, 26 of the 40 results shown missed by 8+ points: efficiency first in 14, finishing drives 5, turnovers 4, nothing stood out 2, defensive/return touchdowns 1. Week 9 had efficiency first in 7 of 26; Week 8 in 15 of 25. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin, defensive/return touchdowns and points per trip inside the 40 with long-run averages, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than Vegas, results are mixed to poor.
lessons.evidence: About 4 of 12 right overall. The only disagreement in the Week 10 results shown was Tulane (model by 3.0, Vegas Tulsa -3); Tulsa won 60-10. Arizona State at UCF (model Arizona State by 0.5, Vegas UCF -3.5) is the open case this week. Sample is small.
lessons.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak.
lessons.evidence: Season: 12 of 30 hit against 15.3 expected, at -7.09 units (was 8 of 22 last run, so 4 of 8 this week). The edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed), so the model's own chance is below break-even on all five picks this week.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Check that each pick's cover chance matches the model's own margin. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Underdog picks have hit a bit less often than the model expected, but long prices have kept units positive.
lessons.evidence: Season: 10 of 29 hit against 11.5 expected, at +1.56 units (was 7 of 22, 8.3 expected, +0.48 units; 3 of 7 hit this week). A few hits swing the units a lot, which shows how much luck is in this list.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%, 45%+). Need 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: Season: 22 of 24 hit against 21.5 expected, at +0.32 units (was 17 of 19; 5 of 5 this week). Prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The model's spread misses are slightly larger than Vegas's over the season.
lessons.evidence: Season (234 games): average spread miss 12.5 points for the model against 11.9 for Vegas, still a 0.6 gap. Winners right in 154 of 234 (66%), spread record 111-117-4. In the 40 Week 10 results shown: 24 of 39 winners and 17-23 against the spread.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, and whether the gap changes by week of season.

lessons.lesson: The idea that the model's margin runs well above Vegas's when a starting QB is out was not supported by this week's results.
lessons.evidence: Kansas State (Week 9) fit the idea: model +9.1 vs Vegas +2.5, lost. But in three flagged Week 10 games the model was closer than Vegas each time: Boise State 64-38 (model by 24.5, Vegas 19.5, actual 26), Oklahoma 23-7 over Florida (model Florida by 2.3, Vegas 5.5, 18.3 vs 21.5 off) and Air Force 24-21 over Army (7.0 vs 8.5 off). 1 of 4 supports it.
lessons.test: On past seasons, flag games where a team's starting QB was out and compare the model's margin error and the Vegas error in those games with all other games. Need 20+ such games.
